books.title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता
books.desc: 18 chapters, 700 verses: Sanskrit, Roman transliteration and Gandhi's Hindi meaning.
books.ocr_note: हिन्दी अर्थ गांधीजी के ‘अनासक्तियोग’ (सस्ता साहित्य मंडल, 1949 संस्करण) से है। यह विकिस्रोत पर स्कैन का OCR पाठ है, जिसकी अभी जाँच (proofreading) नहीं हुई है, इसलिए कहीं-कहीं अक्षर ग़लत हो सकते हैं। हर अर्थ के साथ स्कैन पृष्ठ का लिंक है। The Hindi meaning is unproofread OCR from the Wikisource scan of Gandhi's Anasaktiyoga; some letters may be wrong. Each meaning links to its scan page.

books.title: पराशरस्मृतिः
books.desc: A dharmaśāstra in 12 chapters, all 583 ślokas: Sanskrit, Roman transliteration and a plain-English meaning. Opens one śloka at a time.
about: The Parāśara Smṛti is a dharmaśāstra of twelve chapters, given by the sage Parāśara to his son Vyāsa as the law for the Kali age. The text itself (12.81) says it has 592 ślokas; this edition has 583.

Sanskrit text from Sanskrit Wikisource, used under CC BY-SA 4.0. Verse numbers follow that edition; in chapter 12 the number in brackets is the older numbering. Roman transliteration is generated from the Devanagari.

The English meanings are plain renderings written by Claude directly from the Sanskrit for this reader. They are not a scholarly translation; check a printed edition before relying on a point of law or ritual.
Keys: ← and → turn the page. On a phone, swipe left or right. Type a number such as 3.16 in “Go to” to jump to a śloka.

books.title: रामचरितमानस · बालकाण्ड
books.desc: Tulsidas' Awadhi verses with a Hindi meaning and the editor's notes (Belvedere Press, 1925). Doha 1 to about 290; the rest of Bal Kand is not yet proofread on Wikisource.

books.title: सुन्दरकाण्ड
books.desc: The fifth kand of the Ramcharitmanas, complete except the two opening Sanskrit shlokas (scan page not yet proofread), with Hindi meaning and notes.

sa-parashara.title: पराशरस्मृतिः — संस्कृत पाठ (Sanskrit text)

sa-parashara.note: All 583 ślokas in 12 chapters, copied from the data of the parashara-smriti reader, which took them from the Sanskrit Wikisource chapter pages. Verse numbers follow that edition; in chapter 12 the number in brackets is the older numbering. Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule from the Devanagari.

parashara-en.title: Parāśara Smṛti — plain-English meanings
parashara-en.note: Plain renderings written with Claude directly from the Sanskrit for that reader. They are not a scholarly translation and are not taken from any published translation; check a printed edition before relying on a point of law or ritual.

manas.title: रामचरितमानस (सटीक) — तुलसीदास; टीका महावीरप्रसाद मालवीय ‘वीर’
manas.where: Hindi Wikisource transcription of the Belvedere Press edition, Prayag, 1925.
manas.licence: Public domain (published 1925; tagged PD-1996 on Wikisource); Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA 4.0
manas.note: Tulsidas' text (16th century) is public domain. The 1925 commentary is public domain in the USA (published before 1931) and is hosted on Wikisource as public domain. Only scan pages that Wikisource volunteers have proofread are used; unproofread pages are shown as gaps with a link to the scan. The Roman transliteration is made by a fixed rule.

sa-gita.title: भगवद्गीता — संस्कृत पाठ (Sanskrit text)
sa-gita.note: Verse text only, taken from the 18 chapter pages. The Roman transliteration is made from it by a fixed rule (tools/iast.py).

anasakti.title: अनासक्तियोग — मोहनदास करमचंद गांधी (Hindi meaning)
anasakti.where: Hindi Wikisource scan of the 1949 (6th) edition, Sasta Sahitya Mandal, New Delhi; first published 1929–30. Scan from the Digital Library of India.
anasakti.licence: Public domain in India (PD-India); text pages on Wikisource are CC BY-SA 4.0
anasakti.note: Gandhi died in 1948, so his writings are public domain in India (life + 60 years). The Hindi version is an unnamed rendering of Gandhi's Gujarati, published by Sasta Sahitya Mandal. The text here is the unproofread OCR on Wikisource, used as it stands: only running headers, page numbers, scan noise and Gandhi's notes (टिप्पणी) are left out. Verses 6.42–6.45 (scan page blank), 8.20 and 18.73–18.74 (OCR too damaged) have no meaning.
